messages:
maya: Drafting the product post framing — quick sanity check on the main performance claim. Proposed opener: "Redwood Inference cuts per-token serving cost by ~40% compared to stock LLM hosting, while keeping latency within SLOs." Thoughts?

aj: Do we have a benchmark artifact to back the 40%? Where's the benchmark link?

maya: Short link to our internal doc: https://redwood.internal/bench/2026-03-cost-vs-baseline (will add public repo later). Pasting the quick snippet:
```txt
40% cost reduction vs baseline
p99 latency ~120ms
throughput +1.8x
```

sam: Prefer wording like "up to 40%" or "reduced cost by about 40% in our tests" — avoids overcommit. Also call out the workload (chat vs embeddings).

maya: Good call. New suggestion: "In internal benchmarks on instruction-following chat workloads, Redwood reduced per-token serving cost by up to 40% versus a baseline stock runtime."

elaine: From brand voice: lead with customer impact too — e.g., "Ship new features faster at lower serving costs." But be careful with promises. Legal?

legal-bot: Please upload the reproducibility artifacts: benchmark script, dataset or prompts, commit hash, hardware summary (GPU type, driver, CUDA), and config flags. We can't approve a hard percentage claim without that. Use a footnote for methodology.

maya: Will do. For the public post I propose we use "up to 40%" + parenthetical "(in our internal tests on chat workloads)". OK to proceed with that tone?

linda: Routing/ops note: CTA should funnel to the product webinar sign-up so we capture demos. Set link to /webinars/product-inference and add UTM params: utm_campaign=post-framing-2754&utm_source=blog. Also add a hidden form field to route inbound leads to 'launch-product' SDR queue.

aj: Nit on phrase "stock runtime" — sounds vague. Maybe "baseline open-source runtime configured without batching or KV caching". More precise and defensible.

maya: Revised line: "In internal tests on instruction-following chat workloads, Redwood reduced per-token serving cost by up to 40% compared to a baseline open-source runtime configured without batching or KV cache." Thoughts?

sam: Love the precision. Also propose including a tiny 2-row benchmark table in the post (this test vs baseline) and linking to the full reproducibility repo — helps transparency and legal.

elaine: Design ask: can we get a simple explainer graphic that maps cost vs latency tradeoffs? @design — can you estimate a 2–3 day turnaround? We'll need SVG optimized for blog and a 1200x628 hero.

maya: I'll open a design thread. For approvals, proposed schedule: internal content review by Thu, legal sign-off by Fri (once repo uploaded), final marketing QA by Mon, publish next Wed. Who owns final sign-off? @aj can you take it?

aj: Happy to own final sign-off. Assigning to me. :thumbsup:

legal-bot: Reminder: use "up to X" phrasing plus methodological footnote. Ping when artifacts are uploaded.

maya: Thanks everyone — I'll push the updated draft and benchmark artifacts by EOD and ping legal. Appreciate the quick checks!
